ops.title: Linux port review synthesis: REWORK findings and the decisions taken
ops.body:
Four independent astra reviews (correctness finder, security refuter, Darwin regression, ABWC contract) over a4c43d9..a92416a, synthesized by opus; full text under /Users/yasyf/.local/state/orca-workspace/recovery-20260930/cookiesync-linux/review/ (finder.md, security.md, darwin.md, contract.md, synthesis.md). Verdict REWORK; no security invariant refuted.

Must-fix accepted: M1 WindowAuto collapsed to headed in `rpc bridge_open` and cross-host forwarding; M2 arc as a second local browser in untagged tests (plus a hang on `<-consent.entered`); M3 fixtures without a `meta` table; M4 fixtures not isolating XDG_CONFIG_HOME; M5 remote browser targets validated against the local registry (fix: platform-independent `cookie.BrowserNames` for remote targets); M6 Secret Service lookup across all collections instead of Chrome's ReadAlias("default") collection; M7 uninstall on a never-installed host errors inside daemonkit v0.32.1 inventoryClear (upstream fix: return nil on fs.ErrNotExist); M8 chrome_crashpad leaves the daemonkit session.

Should-fix accepted: S2 target parsing via BrowserNames, S3 scheme_store_test meta case, S4-S6 linux-smoke.sh assertion rigor. Rejected: the Darwin `--headed` help-text change (behavior identical for every flag combination), U6.md wording, duplicates.

Decisions: chromium dropped from the Linux registry (root #116/#133); Chrome discovery on Linux stays PATH-based (same-UID PATH steering is out of scope on a single-user VM; fixed /usr/bin paths would drop user-local installs); the strict reading of #133 applies (Linux never mints the `local` principal, in-process callers included).
